## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `101fd543d0d8e5cf66e8b944dca3b4d9403ff745`
Local-runs: none
Scope: .claude/agents/os-dev.md, .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/SKILL.md, scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs, scripts/pm/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs + scripts/pm/check-half-states.mjs, scripts/pm/check-owed-reviews.mjs, scripts/pm/fleet-write/execute.mjs
Security-touching: yes
Rule-change-verified: none

Read: card #35612 (body and all six comments, the seat's reading 7071055960 included), PR #36215 (body, its seven files, the net diff of 420 added and 44 deleted lines), and the 55 check-runs on this head. The PR's files were read at the head with `git show`; the cited code outside the diff was read, not reviewed. Nothing was built or run.

On the two header lines:

- The security line reads yes and a yes is meant, in the fail-closed sense the line asks for. No `hits` path sits under `skills/**` or `ui/skills/**`, and nothing here teaches product security. But the changed hunks in the two guard files decide which record lets a pull request land without a human approval, and the changed line of the dispatch skill words which pull requests a seat may land itself. That is approval and permission behaviour of the fleet. The line is read by the low-risk skills arm alone, and this pull request is not on that arm.
- The rule-change line reads none, the value the PR body declares. The reasoning is under ④, point 1. This pull request touches two guard instruments, which are Tier H whatever this line reads, so it waits for the maintainer either way.

### ① Derived judgments

Every tier reading the diff moves, each compared with `main`:

- The relay's review plan (`governedReviewPlan`): a `.claude/**` pull request read on its path list alone goes from Tier S to Tier H. It returns to Tier S only on a body declaring `none` or `ruled` and a record the stage verifies. Right. No path makes a plan cheaper than on `main`: the row's raw tier was already S, so the chained split can only keep S or raise to H, and every other row passes through `applyRuleChangeSplit` as the same object.
- The patrol's governed slice (`h43RuleChangeSlice`): the same move, for H43, H48 and H69, which share the slice. Right for H43; see N1 for H48 and H69.
- The split's record conjunct (`ruleChangeRecordReasons`): one more condition, the queue's record leg on the same comment. A record with no leg reading handed in is now Tier H. Right, and stricter only. The three producers of that record object in the tree all hand the leg in: `lowRiskRecordStage`, `ruleChangeRecordVerdict` and `h43RuleChangeRecord`. The `--pr` print gets it through `readLowRiskRecordStage`.
- The queue leg's own verdict is unchanged: `ruleChangeRecordVerdict` hands in the leg it has already judged as standing, so the new condition never fires there.
- The early-warning leg: a split entry can read "Tier H on the body" or "Tier H until its record is read" where it read "Tier H until the PR body is read". It can never read Tier S, because `readPayloadDeclaration` hands in no record and no deferred leg, and `guardVerdict` returns exit 0 for this event before any entry is judged. Right.
- The owed-review list (`owedFace`): a narrowing declared on the `Metadata-protocol:` line alone is now listed at the narrowing face's tier. A body declaring `Clause-②: yes` beside `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` moves from the declaration limb to the narrowing limb, which is the dearer one. No body that was listed before is now unlisted. Right.
- New exports: `readPayloadDeclaration`, `ruleChangeReadable`, `ruleChangeReadingFor`, `ruleChangeReadingText`, `h43RuleChangeSlice`, `h43RuleChangePending`, `h43RuleChangeRecord`, and two more keys on the patrol's register object. All are internal to `scripts/pm`; nothing published moves.

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: no — correct. The diff touches `scripts/pm/**` and two files under `.claude/**`; no package, no published schema and no generated output. The `skip-changeset` label is on the pull request and Check Changeset is green on this head. `Metadata-protocol: none` is right.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Premise correction (the card's done-when says "at `pr_create`"): accepted. The relay summons nobody at `pr_create` by its own header and by line 205 of the dispatch skill, so the request is pinned at `pr_ready`, the only follow-up the relay has.
- Open question, item 4 (the post-merge sweep's split leg): answered by the seat's reading 7071055960. It stays on this card and is built in a second pull request; the body says `Part of #35612`, so the card stays open. Until then every merged `.claude/**` pull request stays on the maintainer's recognition list, which hides no landing.
- Out-of-scope finding (the low-risk arm's record stage does not consult the record leg): folded into the same card by the same reading. The stage now carries `recordLeg` for both arms, so that fix is one condition. Not judged here.
- Deviation, file surface: the claim lists `scripts/pm` files only, and the diff also edits one line in each of two `.claude/**` files (N5 and N6, carried by this card since comment 7031820361). Accepted; both lines are judged under ④.
- Deviation, `main` not merged before the pull request was opened: accepted. The pull request reads mergeable and clean, and the check-runs are on this head.
- Deviations on commit trailers and on `test:repo` left to CI: accepted; the check-runs answer the second.
- Check-runs: 55 on this head, each success or skipped, none failed or pending. Governed Surface Queue Guard, the scoped tooling self-tests, the dispatch-gates lint, the half-state sweep, the governed-merges audit and the PR-body guards are all green.
- SQL push-down: not applicable. The diff holds no query and no data access.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix, no should-fix.

1. The rule-change value, hunk by hunk.
   - `.claude/agents/os-dev.md` line 279 now tells the developer to write exactly one line-start `Rule-change:` line. `readOneBareLine` already holds a body with two such lines as unreadable, which is Tier H. The line states what the reader does and changes nothing an agent may do.
   - `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/SKILL.md` line 208: the skills-lane exception changes from "guards excepted" to "guard instruments excepted". This is the one hunk that needed thought, because the same file uses the shorter word for its index of every check script, so the old wording could be read as excepting all of them. I read the hunk as wording. Line 193 of the same file names the guard instruments as four scripts, the guard workflow, settings and hooks, and it is unchanged. The register holds exactly those rows at Tier H, and it is unchanged. The card records that the maintainer's order on #35321 names four files and that widening the set is his to say. So the wide reading was never the rule in force, and the hunk moves no pull request from the maintainer to a seat.
   - The five script files are scripts, which the brief excludes. They implement the 2026-11-19 ruling at more readers and are stricter at every one of them.
   So `none` is verified. The residual is stated for the maintainer, who approves this pull request anyway: if he did mean line 208 to cover every check script, this hunk narrows it.

2. `scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs`. The new condition sits after the carry check and before the line check. A missing leg has its own reason, and each of the three states has its own words. The header paragraph that said two readers do not chain the split is replaced by one that matches the code. Holds.

3. `scripts/pm/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs`.
   - `lowRiskRecordStage` builds `recordLeg` with the queue's own two functions on the same pair. So the face, the tier name, the single verdict line, the contradicting spellings and the open grades are all the queue's reading. The rows it reads are already cut to trusted authors by `readRecordThreads`. I looked for a caller whose pair would make `recordVerdict` throw or read wrongly, and found none: the queue leg and `readLowRiskRecordStage` both hand in a path list and a repository id, and the one call with a null pull returns before the stage is built.
   - The record leg's reason can quote a record line. `recordPassVerdict` flattens the quote, and a served token of model-identifier shape is never quoted: the below-tier state carries no reason.
   - `readPayloadDeclaration` re-reads the entry's existing surfaces, so a workflow reading on the same entry is kept. On this event the diff is one row attributed to the named pull request, so the payload body cannot be read against another pull request's entry.
   - The value printed in "declares `Rule-change: …`" comes from the reader's closed set, never raw body text.
   - The new words say "this leg reads no record". The branch is reachable only on the early-warning leg: the queue leg always hands in the deferred stage, so its split is never pending.
   - The workflow's `types:` list is `opened, synchronize, reopened, ready_for_review`, as the body says, so a body edit is read by the next push or by the queue leg. Holds.

4. `scripts/pm/fleet-write/execute.mjs`. I tried three ways to make a request go unsent when it is owed.
   - A plan that is Tier S on fewer facts than the queue needs. Not found. The split's Tier S needs a body declaring a seat value and a record the stage verifies, read through `readLowRiskRecordStage` with the guard's own comment reader. `ruleChangeReadable` is a cost gate that can only keep a plan at Tier H.
   - A mixed pull request. `AGENTS.md` beside the wording, a settings or hooks path, a workflow or skills row beside it, and a repository outside `ruleChange.repos` each stay Tier H and request.
   - A later edit. A body edited to `yes` after a clean `pr_ready`, or a newer record that does not verify, is not re-read by the relay. The queue leg refuses such a pull request and H43 lists it, so nothing lands unseen. This matches the card's own statement of the worst case.
   A record carried from an older head is refused here because no checkout is handed in; that costs one extra request. The final plan is rebuilt with the same reading, so the verdict row and the writes agree. Holds.

5. `scripts/pm/check-half-states.mjs`. The body is read off the open-pull list row, which carries it. A register that loads without either new export is refused by the loader with both names in its reason. An unread thread or an unloaded author binding is not measured, so Tier H. Thread reads go through the existing cache. H43's own row cannot fire early: its hand-off needs a trusted PASS on the head on the PR thread, which is the same comment the split's record is read from. Holds for H43. See N1.

6. `scripts/pm/check-owed-reviews.mjs`. `narrowingDeclarationsIn` and `NARROWING_FACE_LINE` are the queue leg's own; the unfilled template menu still declares nothing. The stated bound, that changesets are not read, is real and in the docblock. Holds.

Nits:

- N1 (nit) — `scripts/pm/check-half-states.mjs`, the docblock of `h43RuleChangeRecord`, repeated in the PR body's acceptance notes and in the seat's reading: both bounds are said to err toward standing down. The first one errs the other way. A `.claude/**` pull request declaring `none` whose verified PASS sits on its card thread, or is carried from an older head, reads absent here and stays Tier H in the slice, while the queue lands it Tier S. H43 stays silent in that case, as point 5 says. H48 and H69 read the same slice, so H48 can tell a seat to add the awaiting-merge label and a maintainer brief on such a pull request once it carries an ACCEPT. The patrol is report-only, the records I checked for #35610 sit on the PR thread, and nothing lands differently. Suggested: correct the direction in the docblock, and let the card's second pull request read the record through the guard's locator. Follow-up on #35612; no change needed on this head.
- N2 (nit) — `scripts/pm/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs`, self-test comment above `VERIFIED_STAGE` (near line 4345): it still says the early-warning leg reads no body, "exactly as the live one". The live leg now reads the payload's body. Comment only.

## 维护者速读

- 用户能看到什么变化:用户无感。车队内部:改车队规则文件的 PR 若声明改了规则或没写声明,标记就绪时会自动请你审,每日巡查也会把它列为等你批准;声明未改规则且审核记录核过的,不再打扰你。
- 为什么做:上一轮让「改规则的车队文档要你批」在合并队列生效,但自动请审、每日巡查和几处只读提示还按旧办法读,这次把它们与合并队列对齐。
- 出错会怎样:最多多请你审一次或漏请一次,合并队列那道拦截不变;改动只在车队工具里,可整体撤回。
- 要你做什么:批准本 PR(它改了守卫仪器文件,只能由你批)。合同审查 PASS 记录是评论 7075245087,Head-sha `101fd543d0d8e5cf66e8b944dca3b4d9403ff745`。
- 席位意见:ACCEPT。所有读取器只会把 Tier S 读成 H、不会反向,审查逐条试破未果;卡的第 4 项与一处同形缺陷留在 #35612 第二个 PR。

## 席位核对

- 形态:`l1-face --pr 36215` CLEAN;draft、base `main`、`Part of #35612`(第 4 项与 `lowRiskRecordStageReasons` 一处按席位读数 7071055960 留卡);7 个文件 +420 −44;`skip-changeset` 正确,`Clause-②: no`。
- 前提实测:`.claude/**` 声明拆分已在 main;改动只让各读取器链上同一拆分,不新增门禁;两行技能文字均在字节上限内,上限行未动。
- 门禁 check-runs @ `101fd543d0d8e5cf66e8b944dca3b4d9403ff745`:32 success · 23 expected skip · 0 failed · 0 pending。dev 本地 78 族 77 过、1 族前置未满足(CI 覆盖)。
- 接受的偏差:合同审查 7075245087 的 N1(`h43RuleChangeRecord` 文档说两界都偏向不报,实有一界偏向多报)与 N2(守卫自测注释过时)作接受的偏差,N1 随 #35612 第二个 PR 修。`Security-touching: yes` 为有意(守卫决定哪条记录可免人批),本 PR 不走低风险臂。
- 范围外去向:第 4 项(合并后审计拆分腿)与低风险臂记录腿缺陷 → #35612 第二个 PR(7071055960)。
- 落地条款:Tier H(守卫仪器 ×2)。L2 PASS 在案,无未闭 must-fix/should-fix ⇒ 挂 `pm:awaiting-merge`、请 os-zhuang 审批;获批后席位落地。
